subject: POC trial planning follow-up / workload intake - FintechX
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning follow-up / workload intake - FintechX

Hi Lisa — great speaking earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC:

Summary of call
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for FintechX conversational fraud detection assistant (NLP rescoring + response generation).
- Success criteria (initial):
  - <90ms p95 end-to-end token latency for 512-token requests under baseline concurrency (see below)
  - Model quality: F1 >= 0.82 on your evaluation set (scoring evaluation to be run by FintechX)
  - Cost target: average per-1000-token cost under $X (we'll size once we have traffic profile)

Workload / intake items I asked for during the call (please confirm):
- Average RPS: baseline 12 RPS, peak 120 RPS (burst to 200 for <10s)
- Avg token length: 220 tokens; 95th percentile 520 tokens
- Typical concurrency: baseline 8 concurrent open requests, peak 80
- Burst patterns: morning batch job spikes + product launch bursts (5–10x for seconds-to-minutes)

Proposed next steps
1) You share the sample payloads + evaluation set (redacted) — Marissa will use these to generate an initial sizing and config.
2) We build a 2-week POC environment (dedicated tenant) with telemetry and cost estimates — target start: week of Apr 19.
3) Mutual Action Plan (attached): owners, timelines, deliverables.

Ownership: Ben (sales) — program lead / procurement; Marissa (SE) — technical lead / sizing; FintechX: Lisa (product) & Samuel (eng) as internal owners.

Can you confirm the workload numbers above and attach the sample payloads and evaluation set? I attached a draft Mutual_Action_Plan_FintechX.xlsx for you to review.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial planning follow-up / workload intake - FintechX

Thanks Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers (approx):
- Baseline RPS: 10–15 RPS (avg ~12)
- Sustained peak: ~120 RPS for sustained marketing periods (minutes)
- Bursts: short spikes up to 200–250 RPS for <10–30s (we see these during campaign rollouts)
- Avg token length: 200–250 tokens; 95p ~500–600 tokens
- Concurrency: baseline 6–10 (avg 8), typical peak concurrency ~70–90

Evaluation plan/timeline:
- Week 1 (Apr 19–23): environment setup + sample runs; Marissa to validate end-to-end latency on sample payloads.
- Week 2 (Apr 26–30): run evaluation set (we will score and return metrics), run 2 controlled burst tests.
- Acceptance: we will sign off if latency & quality targets are met and no functional regressions.

Owners:
- FintechX: Lisa Chen (product lead), Samuel Ortiz (eng lead) — Samuel will provide payloads & coordinate redacted eval set.
- Redwood: Ben (AE), Marissa (SE)

I attached sample_payloads.jsonl (redacted) in the next email; Samuel will send the full eval set once legal confirms the NDA scope.

—Lisa
Lisa Chen
Director, Product — FintechX
lisa@fintechx.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial planning follow-up / workload intake - FintechX

Thanks Lisa — this looks great and aligns with what we heard. A couple of quick clarifying questions before Marissa sizes the environment:

1) Tokenization: are the token counts based on byte-pair tokenization similar to OpenAI/LLM tokenizers, or are they character counts? If you have a few representative strings (we can run a tokenizer locally) that will help.
2) For the burst patterns: are the 200–250 RPS bursts typically distributed across many users (fan-out) or concentrated to a few long-running sessions?
3) Can Samuel confirm whether any requests include attachments (base64 small files) or long context windows > 2k tokens?

If it's easy, Samuel/FintechX can drop a short sample of the longest expected context (redacted) in the ticket or as an inline reply. Once we have that Marissa will share a recommended instance/class and an initial throughput/cost estimate.

I'll update the Mutual_Action_Plan with the clarified owners/timeline and re-share.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: POC trial planning follow-up / workload intake - FintechX

Thanks all — I pulled together an initial sizing based on the provided numbers and a few assumptions below. Attaching sample_payloads.jsonl (sanitized) for my throughput tests.

Sizing notes (rough):
- Target model: redwood/retina-medium-8k (quantized) for cost/latency balance.
- Baseline throughput target: p95 < 90ms for 512-token requests at baseline concurrency (8) — achievable on 1x A100-class instance with our optimized runtime for the provided samples.
- Peak & burst testing: to sustain 120 RPS with bursts to 250 for short windows, I'll provision a 3-node pool and validate autoscaling policies. We may need burst buffer or batching tweaks to avoid queuing delays during <30s spikes.
- Tokenization: I ran the supplied sample payloads against our tokenizer — your 95p ~550 tokens maps to ~520–580 subword tokens for the retin a tokenizer we use. Please confirm if you preprocess prompts server-side (e.g., adding metadata or long system prompts).

Requests for FintechX:
- Samuel: please confirm if you add any per-request attachments or additional metadata (headers) we should account for.
- Please provide 5–10 of the longest real requests (redacted) so I can validate p95 latency under realistic tails.

I'll update the Mutual_Action_Plan with a proposed 2-week runbook and the resource plan after I complete a dry run this week.

Attachments: sample_payloads.jsonl (10 lines, redacted request texts)

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — confirmed. We don't send attachments in-request; it's all JSON payloads. Bursts are fan-out across users (many concurrent short requests), not long-running sessions.

I've uploaded the redacted eval set to our shared S3 (link in HubSpot comment) and asked Legal to expedite the NDA for the full dataset. Lisa will own the acceptance once the evaluation run completes.

We'll be ready to hit the Apr 19 start window. Samuel (eng) will be the main contact for technical handoffs.

Best,
Sam
